math_review: The full ring of integers of Q(sqrt(10)) gives a complete elementary negative answer to the equality printed in Long Question 7.2 (arXiv:1512.04620v1), using its prime-element convention and without a PID assumption. Both the unit-difference and unit-or-prime-element-difference graphs have clique number two, and the least norm of a nonzero prime ideal is two. The displayed proposed equality therefore compares two with four.
priority_scope: This is a credited elementary exposition, with no claim of novelty, firstness, current worldwide openness, or independent discovery lineage. Lenstra's 1977 Proposition 2.2 already supplies the ideal-residue unit-clique bound. Dummit's 2021 notes explicitly contain the same classical ideal and norm obstruction. Long and Thistlethwaite supply the prime-clique framework; Lopez's 2018 thesis defines the same first prime graph and related higher prime-ideal-power graphs. Combining old ingredients here is not backdated as an earlier printed resolution. The exact historical priority of the full graph conclusion remains unestablished after the scoped audit.
